chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the kurr of water: how much is its measure?
He عليه السلام said: When the water is three and a half spans by the like of it, and three and a half spans in its depth in the ground, then that is the kurr of water.

key_terms.الْكُرِّ: the legally defined large quantity of water used in rulings of ritual purity
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the subject of the legal measurement in this narration
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَشْبَارٍ: three spans, a unit of physical measurement
key_terms.فِي الْأَرْضِ: in the ground, describing the setting of the measured water
key_terms.وَنِصْفًا: and a half, completing the stated dimension

ai.seo_question: What is the measured amount of kurr water in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal measure of kurr water by specifying its dimensions in length, width, and depth. It is significant in jurisprudence because the quantity of kurr water is a foundational criterion in rulings of ritual purity and impurity.
